evidence.quote: However, I expect most of this increase to be transitory and for inflation to return to—or perhaps run somewhat above—our 2 percent longer-run goal in 2022 and 2023.
We expect to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes—as well as our maximum-employment mandate—are achieved.
the true unemployment rate is closer to 10 percent.

a low unemployment rate, in and of itself, will not be sufficient to trigger a tightening of monetary policy absent any evidence from other indicators that inflation is at risk of moving above mandate-consistent levels.
We are committed to using our full range of tools to support the economy until the job is well and truly done to help ensure that the economic recovery will be as robust and rapid as possible.
we will continue to increase our holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and our holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $40 billion per month

parsed.rationale: Despite an upgraded growth outlook, the speaker treats the inflation rise as transitory, stresses remaining labor market slack, and reaffirms patient, accommodative rate and asset-purchase guidance. The net signal is dovish, though it mostly restates existing guidance rather than signaling new easing.
